verdicts.decision_note: The client requires NFT metadata to render separate Small Block and Big Block ticket counters plus permanent badges.
The client specifies that the NFT mint number is the referral code rendered in its on-chain metadata.
Eliminating Big Blocks necessarily removes the existing Big Block ticket counter from NFT metadata.
First concrete failure showing inconsistent NFT-level earnings and ticket attributes.
Target-specific implementation claim that NFT referral, ticket, and earnings details were corrected.
First concrete failure of the NFT referral-code attribute, which displayed the purchase code instead of the NFT's own mint number.
Target-specific implementation claim that the Referral Code attribute now uses the NFT's own token ID.
The generic confirmation follows a request to check multiple fixes and does not unambiguously identify the referral-code attribute.
The client defines the NFT-attribute accounting rule for randomly assigned tickets and commissions, including the required one-ticket-to-one-commission relationship.
The client removes the data-backfill acceptance condition while retaining correct NFT reward attributes for future activity.
Post-fix evidence shows a distinct stale-metadata failure: NFT attributes disagreed with the correct leaderboard and detail values.
Target-specific implementation claim that NFT attributes now use live on-chain metadata as their authoritative source.
First concrete client confirmation after refreshing and checking the target-specific metadata-source fix.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
So far, we have done 12 mints, that should equal 12 tickets & 12 x $5 commissions.

**When there is no referral code used, there is still a ticket and commission**.

Right now, **when a code is used**, it is correctly accounted for on the leaderboards/NFT attributes. Perfect.

When there is **no referral code used**, the ticket and commission are randomly assigned.
(B**ut they still need to be accounted for on the leaderboard/NFT attributes**.)

I think since your last fix, (on the last 2 mints) the randomly assigned tickets have been accounted for on the leaderboard/NFT attributes. Great.
But they have not been backfilled to show the missing tickets.

And the commissions (from these no code buys) are still not being accounted for on the leaderboard/NFT attributes.

In my screenshot you'll see i have an NFT with 2 tickets and only 1 x $5 commission - this should be impossible, as every ticket comes with a $5 commission.

And on my leaderboard screenshot, you can count (from 12 total mints) 7 tickets and 5 x $5 commissions accounted for.
12 mints should equal 12 tickets and 12 x $5 commissions, regardless of a referral code being used or not.

execution.observed_behavior: An NFT displayed two tickets but only one $5 commission, showing that randomly assigned no-referral rewards were not fully reflected in its attributes.

missing_event_candidates.decision_note: Distinct no-referral execution path showing a concrete NFT-attribute accounting failure.
